safety_verdicts.content: Chest pain radiates to the shoulder and neck.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated includes radiation to left arm/shoulder but does not document radiation to the neck as specified in the Gold fact (History_of_Present_Illness-001 lacks neck radiation).
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Radiation of chest discomfort to the neck is a supportive feature for ACS and can increase perceived clinical risk; omitting it may slightly understate symptom severity/pattern in handover or documentation. However, other high-risk features (central pressure, diaphoresis, SOB, nausea, left arm/shoulder radiation) are documented and the emergency response was already initiated.

safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated does not state haemodynamic stability; instead notes no vitals/exam performed (Physical_Findings-001).
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Haemodynamic stability is an important discriminator in suspected MI (e.g., shock/instability changes urgency and management), and its absence can reduce clarity for downstream clinicians. In this encounter, no vitals were recorded and an ambulance was already being arranged, so the omission mainly affects completeness rather than altering immediate care.

safety_verdicts.content: Urgent ECG and troponin T are required.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated mentions ECG on arrival but does not include troponin T testing requirement (Plan_of_Care-003 lacks troponin).
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Troponin testing is a core component of ACS evaluation; omitting it from the plan could reduce clarity in documentation and handover about required investigations. In practice, ED/ambulance pathways for suspected MI will still obtain troponins, so the likely harm is limited to resolution loss rather than missed care.
